subject.title: Reject unsupported diagnostics OTel grpc config

question: Should OpenClaw remove the shipped `diagnostics.otel.protocol: "grpc"` config value now, with doctor removing the field and disabling active OTLP signals, instead of keeping `grpc` accepted until real gRPC export exists?
rationale: The PR is a coherent bug fix, but it deliberately changes upgrade behavior for existing configs and that compatibility policy is a maintainer decision rather than an automated repair choice.

options.title: Accept doctor-backed removal
options.body: Merge after normal exact-head gates, with `grpc` rejected in config and doctor preserving the previous no-export outcome for active OTLP signals.

options.title: Keep schema compatibility
options.body: Pause or close this PR and keep `grpc` accepted until maintainers sponsor real gRPC exporter support or a different migration policy.

options.title: Revise migration semantics
options.body: Ask for a small PR update if maintainers want doctor to preserve, disable, or warn about legacy configs differently.

recommendation.title: Accept doctor-backed removal
recommendation.body: Merge after normal exact-head gates, with `grpc` rejected in config and doctor preserving the previous no-export outcome for active OTLP signals.

likelyOwner.reason: The earliest exporter/config surface and the runtime legacy migration structure both trace to this history, making this the best available routing owner for the compatibility choice.
